# Fuzzy Output Interpretation & Boundary Robustness — `worktree-fuzzy-output-interpretation`

> **Branch scope.** The full study pipeline: the `fuzzypharma` package, a
> single-command runner, and Tasks A–I covering prediction, fuzzification,
> interpretation, rules and temporal consistency. This is the largest branch in the
> project. For the overall overview, see the `main` branch.

Part of *Explainable Fuzzy Machine Learning for Long-Acting Injectables*.

**All artifacts are generated by `python run_study.py` into `study_results/`
(30 files). The full report is in [`RESULTS_SUMMARY.md`](RESULTS_SUMMARY.md).**

---

## Read this first

The study's contribution is **interpretability and boundary robustness of the
predicted release**, *not* predictive accuracy.

- **Tasks A–F** answer the accuracy question — largely: **fuzzy does not help**.
- **Tasks G–I** answer the questions the project is actually about.

See `CHANGES.md` for what was corrected and why, `COLLABORATOR_CHECKLIST.md` for open
questions needing a domain answer, and `proposal.md` for the framing.

Results are organised against five evaluation questions:
**A** predictive performance (Task D) · **B** boundary robustness (Task G) ·
**C** interpretability (Task G) · **D** rule usefulness (Task H) ·
**E** temporal consistency (Task H).

---

## Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Rows | 4,913 measurements → 4,909 after same-time averaging |
| Formulations | 321 |
| Drug groups (exact SMILES) | 88 |
| Split | `GroupKFold(5)` on exact `Drug SMILES` |
| Drugs appearing in > 1 fold | **0** (verified) |
| Missing values | 0 — no imputation |
| Release clipping / monotonicity forcing | none |
| Predictor | XGBoost, one fixed **untuned** config, seed 42, identical in every arm |

Fuzzy knots, the crisp scaler and the classification undersampler are fitted on the
**training fold only**. For the measurement-level task they are fitted on the training
fold's **formulation** rows, not its measurement rows, so a 48-point curve does not
pull the quantiles ten times harder than a 5-point curve.

`Drug` name, `Drug SMILES` and `DOI` are used for grouping and provenance only —
never as model inputs.

---

## Selected findings

### Task C — what fuzzification actually did

Triangular Low/Medium/High with shoulders at q25/q50/q75, refit inside each fold.

A **tied-knot fallback** is declared and fired on exactly the two features the audit
predicted: `LA/GA` (71% one value) and `Solubility Enhancer Concentration` (64%
exactly zero). No feature was unfuzzifiable in any fold.

**Saturation** — share of held-out rows with High membership exactly 1:

| feature | quantile knots | equal-width knots |
|---|---|---|
| Initial Drug-to-Polymer Ratio | 0.430 | 0.003 |
| Polymer MW | 0.318 | 0.009 |
| LA/GA | 0.277 | 0.012 |
| Drug TPSA | 0.265 | 0.022 |
| Particle Size | 0.256 | 0.003 |
| Drug MW | 0.247 | 0.003 |

Quantile shoulders flatten the top quartile of every long-tailed feature into one
label — `Polymer MW` from 46 to 215 becomes indistinguishable. Equal-width knots
remove that, but only by pushing nearly all mass into `Low`, which is a different
distortion rather than a fix. **Both are run as arms.**

### Task D — accuracy (abridged)

| time setting | target | representation | RMSE | Pearson r | R² |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| time-dependent | Release (pointwise) | crisp | 0.2352 ± 0.0430 | 0.7227 | 0.4686 |
| time-dependent | Release (pointwise) | **fuzzy (uniform)** | **0.2294 ± 0.0442** | 0.7331 | 0.4917 |
| time-independent | Release_24h | crisp | 0.2000 ± 0.0329 | 0.2298 | −0.2547 |
| time-independent | Release_24h | **fuzzy (quantile)** | **0.1845 ± 0.0406** | 0.3456 | −0.0402 |

Note the sign of R² in the time-independent block.

---

## Conclusion — did fuzzy representation help?

The question has to be split, because the answers differ.

**As a feature encoding (question A): mostly no.** In the time-dependent setting —
the only setting where the models work at all (R² ≈ 0.47–0.49) — every fuzzy and
hybrid arm lands within **0.006 RMSE** of crisp with win counts of 2/5 to 4/5, which
is noise. Quantile fuzzification did improve the time-independent targets in 5/5 folds
at 24 h and 48 h (Δ ≈ 0.016–0.018, ≈8%), but **every arm there has negative mean R²**:
fuzzification made a failing model fail less. Fuzzy-as-feature-representation is not
clearly earning its complexity.

**As an output interpretation (questions B and C): yes, within measured limits.**
36.9% of held-out predictions receive a graded description; the 4.0% of predictions
sitting within one percentage point of a cut point change their description by 0.057
instead of being reassigned wholesale. That contrast holds under every boundary
definition tried. The honest bound is equally clear: **the layer does nothing for the
other 96%**, and how many formulations fall in the affected 4% is a property of
boundaries nobody has yet validated.

**As a source of rules (question D): no.** Zero rules reached the top tier.

## Repository layout

```text
├── run_study.py                 # Single entry point — regenerates study_results/
├── fuzzypharma/                 # The study package
│   ├── config.py                #   seeds and constants
│   ├── data.py                  #   loading, same-time averaging, provenance
│   ├── folds.py  grouped_cv.py  #   drug-grouped splitting
│   ├── fuzzy.py                 #   membership functions and knot fitting
│   ├── features.py  targets.py  #   feature and target construction
│   ├── phases.py                #   release-phase partitioning
│   ├── modeling.py  pipeline.py #   XGBoost arms, fold loop
│   ├── interpret.py             #   SHAP and graded output interpretation
│   ├── rules.py                 #   rule extraction and held-out validation
│   └── study.py                 #   Task A-I orchestration
├── study_results/               # 30 generated CSV/PNG artifacts
├── RESULTS_SUMMARY.md           # Full generated report
├── CHANGES.md                   # What was corrected, and why
├── COLLABORATOR_CHECKLIST.md    # Open questions needing a domain answer
├── proposal.md                  # Research context and methodology
├── mp_dataset_initial.xlsx      # Source dataset and metadata
└── mp_dataset_processed.xlsx    # Numeric modeling dataset
```

## Reproducing

```bash
python run_study.py
```

Regenerates every file in `study_results/`. The leakage self-check must pass before
any result is reported.

## Related branches

- `worktree-fuzzy-classification` — boundary robustness for the **AUC class** output.
- `worktree-membership-functions` — leakage-free membership functions in isolation.
- `worktree-rule-validation-study` — validates the 8 predefined rules on unseen drugs.
  Consistent with Task H here, its four pure-`Time` rules are unsupported; unlike the
  null result here, the two **Polymer MW** rules do replicate in 5 of 5 held-out folds.

## Constraints (binding)

- Do not present membership boundaries as pharmaceutical truth.
- Do not treat the mathematical AUC class as a clinical burst-release label.
- Do not describe a crisp decision tree as a fuzzy inference system.
- Distinguish candidate / replicated / validated at every mention of a rule.
- Report negative and insignificant results honestly.
